title: Catecholamine tumor with neuroendocrine granules (synaptophysin/chromogranin): adrenal medulla (pheochromocytoma)
vignette: A 40-year-old woman is evaluated for intermittent headaches, insomnia, diaphoresis, and unintentional weight loss over the past several months. The patient has no other medical problems and takes no medications. She does not use tobacco, alcohol, or illicit drugs and has no significant family history. The patient is found to have a neoplastic mass producing excessive amounts of hormones that are causing her symptoms. Surgical resection of the abnormal tissue is performed with no operative complications. Microscopic examination of the tumor cells shows electron-dense, membrane-bound secretory granules. Immunohistochemistry is positive for synaptophysin, chromogranin, and neuron-specific enolase. The abnormal tissue most likely originated from which of the following?

clues.text: intermittent headaches, insomnia, diaphoresis, and unintentional weight loss
clues.note: Episodic headache, sweating, and palpitations with weight loss are classic symptoms of catecholamine excess (pheochromocytoma).
Dense-core neurosecretory granules on electron microscopy are typical of neuroendocrine cells that store catecholamines - the chromaffin cells.

clues.text: positive for synaptophysin, chromogranin, and neuron-specific enolase
clues.note: Synaptophysin, chromogranin, and neuron-specific enolase are NEUROENDOCRINE markers; together with catecholamine symptoms they identify chromaffin cells of the ADRENAL MEDULLA (pheochromocytoma).

whatMatters: Episodic catecholamine symptoms + a tumor with dense-core neurosecretory granules staining for SYNAPTOPHYSIN, CHROMOGRANIN, and NEURON-SPECIFIC ENOLASE = a PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA, which arises from the CHROMAFFIN cells of the ADRENAL MEDULLA. Answer B.
strategy: Combine the clinical (catecholamine excess: headache, sweating, palpitations) with the pathology (neuroendocrine markers + dense-core granules) to localize to the adrenal MEDULLA (chromaffin cells). Reject adrenal cortex (steroid tumors: Cushing/hyperaldosteronism/virilization), ovary (sex-steroid tumors), parathyroid (hypercalcemia), and thyroid follicles (thyroid hormone, follicular architecture) - none produce catecholamines with these neuroendocrine markers.

eliminations.label: Adrenal cortex - steroid, not catecholamine tumors
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: cortical tumors producing STEROID hormones (cortisol, aldosterone, androgens). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: they cause hypercortisolism/hyperaldosteronism/virilization and show well-developed smooth ER, not dense-core catecholamine granules or neuroendocrine markers. ✅ Correct if: Cushing syndrome, Conn syndrome, or virilization.

eliminations.label: Ovary - sex-steroid tumors
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: ovarian hormone-producing tumors (estrogen/androgen). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: these cause hyperestrogenism or virilization, not catecholamine excess with chromaffin markers. ✅ Correct if: estrogen/androgen-secreting ovarian tumor.

eliminations.label: Parathyroid - hypercalcemia
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: parathyroid adenoma/carcinoma producing PTH. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it causes hypercalcemia (stones, bones, groans), not catecholamine symptoms; not a chromaffin tumor. ✅ Correct if: primary hyperparathyroidism with hypercalcemia.

eliminations.label: Thyroid follicles - thyroid hormone, follicular
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a thyroid follicular tumor producing thyroid hormone. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it shows follicular architecture with colloid, not dense-core catecholamine granules; (medullary thyroid carcinoma is neuroendocrine but arises from parafollicular C cells, not follicular cells, and secretes calcitonin). ✅ Correct if: thyroid hormone excess with follicular histology.

reasoning: Episodic headache, diaphoresis, palpitations = catecholamine excess
Dense-core neurosecretory granules + synaptophysin/chromogranin/NSE = neuroendocrine (chromaffin) tumor
Chromaffin cells that secrete catecholamines reside in the adrenal medulla
-> pheochromocytoma of the adrenal medulla; answer B
mechanism: PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA is a tumor of the CHROMAFFIN CELLS of the ADRENAL MEDULLA that overproduces CATECHOLAMINES (norepinephrine, epinephrine, dopamine). Fluctuating catecholamine release causes episodic HEADACHE, DIAPHORESIS, PALPITATIONS/tachycardia, and HYPERTENSION, often with weight loss; diagnosis is confirmed by elevated urinary/plasma catecholamines and METANEPHRINES. Histology shows nests of chromaffin cells; the neurosecretory nature is confirmed by ELECTRON-DENSE, membrane-bound (dense-core) secretory GRANULES and positive immunostaining for NEUROENDOCRINE markers - SYNAPTOPHYSIN, CHROMOGRANIN, and NEURON-SPECIFIC ENOLASE. About 25% are inherited (VHL, MEN2/RET, NF1), and the 'rule of 10s' applies (10% bilateral, extra-adrenal, malignant). The other options produce different hormones with different histology: adrenal cortex (steroids, smooth ER), ovary (sex steroids), parathyroid (PTH/hypercalcemia), and thyroid follicles (thyroid hormone, follicular architecture).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Endo > pheochromocytoma: chromaffin cells of adrenal medulla; catecholamine excess (episodic HTN, headache, sweating, palpitations); urinary/plasma metanephrines; chromogranin/synaptophysin/NSE positive; rule of 10s; VHL/MEN2/NF1.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Catecholamine symptoms + neuroendocrine markers + dense-core granules = adrenal medulla (pheochromocytoma).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on chromaffin cells, catecholamines, synaptophysin/chromogranin/NSE, metanephrines, or neuroendocrine tumor? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Cortex = steroids; ovary = sex steroids; parathyroid = PTH/calcium; thyroid follicles = thyroid hormone (follicular).

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: pheochromocytoma = adrenal medulla chromaffin cells; chromogranin/synaptophysin positive; measure metanephrines; rule of 10s.

firstAid.detail: Endo: adrenal medulla chromaffin cells; catecholamines; chromogranin/synaptophysin.

memoryHook: Sweats, headaches, and a racing heart from a tumor full of dense catecholamine granules (chromogranin+) points to the adrenal MEDULLA - a pheochromocytoma.
